newsitem.title: USA: Clinton decides to certify Mexico - officials.
newsitem.headline: Clinton decides to certify Mexico - officials.

text.p: President Bill Clinton decided on Friday to certify Mexico as a U.S. partner in the war on drugs, officials said.

Clinton also decided to continue U.S. disapproval of Colombia as not helping fight drug-trafficking. The decisions were to be announced by Secretary of State Madeleine Albright at a 4:30 p.m. EST (2130 GMT) news conference.
Clinton's decision to certify Mexico meant that the United States' southern neighbour would avoid a cut-off in some U.S. aid and the possibility of economic sanctions.
It came despite outrage expressed by 40 U.S. senators who said that Mexico had failed in its counter-narcotics efforts and the government and national police suffered from corruption.
On Colombia, Clinton's decision again to deny Colombia certification had been anticipated.
Washington has accused Colombian President Ernesto Samper of accepting millions of dollars from drug traffickers to finance his campaign in 1994.
